options.why: Leaf changes its f to v before adding -es.
The f changes to v before the ending.

hints: Leaf ends in f.
Many words ending in f change the f to v and add -es.
Think of half and halves.
items.explanation: Leaf ends in f, so we change the f to v and add -es: leaves.

hints: Shelf ends in f.
Change the f to v.
Then add the same ending as in leaves.
items.explanation: Shelf changes f to v and adds -es: shelves.

items.prompt: Match each word to its plural.
hints: These words change in other ways to make a plural.
Say each one aloud: one child, two ...
Start with foot. What do you call two of them?
items.explanation: These are irregular plurals. They change inside the word or become a new word, like child and children.

items.prompt:
Write the plural of loaf.
The baker took six ___ of bread out of the oven.
hints: Loaf ends in f.
Words like leaf and loaf change the f.
Change the f to v, then add the ending.
items.explanation: Loaf ends in f, so it becomes loaves.

items.prompt: Sort the words by how they make their plural.
hints: Say each plural aloud.
Do you hear a v sound in the plural?
Start with roof. Do we say roofs or rooves today?
items.explanation: Wolf, half, life and calf change to -ves. Roof, chef, cliff and giraffe just add -s.

items.prompt: There are many ___ in the farmer's field.

options.why: Sheep stays the same for one or many.
There is no -es. The word never changes.

hints: Some animals have the same word for one and for many.
Think of one fish, two fish.
Which word does not change at all?
items.explanation: Sheep is the same in the singular and the plural: one sheep, many sheep.

options.why: Tomato does not end in y.

hints: Tomato ends in o.
Some words ending in o add -es.
Think of potato and potatoes.
items.explanation: Tomato adds -es: tomatoes. Potato and hero do the same.

items.prompt:
Write the plural of goose.
A family of ___ walked across the road.
hints: Goose has an irregular plural.
Think of tooth and teeth.
Change the oo sound in the middle.
items.explanation: Goose has an irregular plural, geese, just like tooth becomes teeth.

items.prompt: Which sentence has every plural spelt correctly?

options.text: The childs put the loaves on the shelfs.
options.why: Child becomes children, and shelf becomes shelves.

options.text: The children put the loafs on the shelves.
The childrens put the loaves on the shelves.
options.why: Children is already plural. It does not need an s.

options.text: The children put the loaves on the shelves.

hints: There are three plurals in each sentence.
Check the plural of child, then loaf, then shelf.
Remember that some plurals do not end in s at all.
items.explanation: Child becomes children, loaf becomes loaves and shelf becomes shelves.

items.prompt:
Write the plurals of calf and pony.
Two ___ and three ___ ate grass in the field.
hints: You need two plurals.
Calf ends in f. Pony ends in a consonant and y.
Do calf first. What happens to the f?
items.explanation: Calf changes f to v: calves. Pony changes y to i and adds -es: ponies.

items.prompt: Choose all the words that are the same in the singular and the plural.
hints: Say each word with one and then with two.
Does the word change at all?
Try sheep: one sheep, two ...?
items.explanation: Sheep, fish and deer stay the same: one deer, two deer. Goat and cow add -s.

items.prompt: Which word breaks the -ves rule and just adds -s?
hints: All four words end in f.
Say each plural aloud.
Listen for a v sound. Which plural keeps an f sound instead?
items.explanation: Roof just adds -s: roofs. Loaf, half and wolf change f to v and add -es.
